L1384: Factors Affecting Operating Results
L1385: General
L1386: Our operating results are largely dependent on the continued popularity and/or on-ice competitiveness of the Rangers, which have a direct effect on ticket sales for the team’s home games and are the team’s largest single source of revenue. Furthermore, success in the regular season may qualify the Rangers for participation in post-season playoffs, which provides us with a significant source of additional revenue, operating income and adjusted operating income. As with other sports teams, the competitive position of the Rangers depends primarily on our ability to develop, obtain and retain talented players, for which we compete with other professional hockey teams.

Waiver and termination costs reflect our efforts to improve the competitiveness of the Rangers. These transactions can result in significant charges as the Company recognizes the estimated ultimate costs of these events in the period in which they occur, although amounts due to these individuals are generally paid over their remaining contract terms. We expect to continue to pursue opportunities to improve the overall quality of the Rangers and our efforts may result in continued significant expenses and charges. Such expenses and charges may result in future operating losses although it is not possible to predict their timing or amount. L10: - MSG Rangers Corp. (NYSE: MSGR) ("MSG Rangers" or the "Company") today reported financial results for the fiscal first quarter ended September 30, 2026. L27: For the fiscal 2027 first quarter, revenues of $14.1 million increased $0.4 million, or 3%, as compared to the prior year period. L32: MSG Rangers Corp. L34: Non-GAAP Financial Measures
L35: We define adjusted operating income (loss), which is a non-GAAP financial measure, as operating income (loss) excluding (i) depreciation, amortization and impairments of property and equipment, goodwill and other intangible assets, (ii) share-based compensation expense or benefit, (iii) restructuring charges or credits, (iv) gains or losses on sales or dispositions of businesses, and (v) the impact of purchase accounting adjustments related to business acquisitions. Because it is based upon operating income (loss), adjusted operating income (loss) also excludes interest expense (including cash interest expense) and other non-operating income and expense items. We believe that the exclusion of share-based compensation expense or benefit allows investors to better track the performance of our business without regard to the settlement of an obligation that is not expected to be made in cash.
L36: We believe adjusted operating income (loss) is an appropriate measure for evaluating the operating performance of our Company. Adjusted operating income (loss) and similar measures with similar titles are common performance measures used by investors and analysts to analyze our performance. Internally, we use revenues and adjusted operating income (loss) as the most important indicators of our business performance, and evaluate management’s effectiveness with specific reference to these indicators. Adjusted operating income (loss) should be viewed as a supplement to and not a substitute for operating income (loss), net income (loss), cash flows from operating activities, and other measures of performance and/or liquidity presented in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). Since adjusted operating income (loss) is not a measure of performance calculated in accordance with GAAP, this measure may not be comparable to similar measures with similar titles used by other companies. For a reconciliation of operating income (loss) to adjusted operating income (loss), please see page 5 of this earnings release.

Customers include fans, suite licensees, sponsors and broadcasters. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, event-related revenue was $5.176 million, sponsorship/signage/suites $4.123 million, league distributions and other $2.950 million, and media rights $1.840 million (10-Q, L761–767; revenue definitions at L775–777).

business_model.claim: Business momentum is mixed: total revenue increased 3% year over year to $14.089 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026. League-distribution revenue increased $1.167 million, primarily from distributions unrelated to national media rights, while other revenue changes offset part of that gain (10-Q, L1414–1423). This is not evidence of broad-based ticket demand growth.

recent_developments.claim: The separation completed on October 26, 2026, after the reported quarter (10-Q, L1478). Subsequent liquidity included a $19.095 million cash contribution in October and $40.905 million of collections related to deferred suite and sponsorship revenue following separation (10-Q, L1481). These receipts improve funding but are not evidence of newly earned revenue.

recent_developments.claim: Most important disclosed risk: Personnel and overhead costs can overwhelm modest revenue growth. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, SG&A increased 26% to $28.088 million, including $3.554 million of separation expenses and $1.358 million of higher compensation and benefits (10-Q, L1447). Direct operating expenses increased 145% to $8.802 million, including $3.064 million of additional personnel-transaction provisions (10-Q, L1425–1434). Separation costs and season-start timing explain part of the deterioration, so the quarter should not be treated as a normalized expense run rate.
recent_developments.quote: Selling, general and administrative expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased $5,802, or 26%, to $28,088 as compared to the prior year period primarily driven by expenses related to the Distribution of $3,554 and higher employee compensation and related benefits of $1,358.

limitations: Historical results are carve-out statements, not an observed standalone operating history. Management says actual standalone costs cannot practicably be quantified (10-Q, L703–716).
Seasonality limits annualization: revenue is disproportionately earned during the fiscal second and third quarters, when most games are played (10-Q, L1515–1516).

Attendance, ticket renewal rates, customer counts, market share and quantified pricing power are not stated in the supplied filings; franchise reputation alone does not establish competitive superiority.

Remaining performance obligations exclude contracts originally lasting one year or less and specified variable consideration, so they are neither a complete revenue forecast nor a measure of cash already collected (10-Q, L805–807).
Regional sports-network solvency and affiliate performance are disclosed risks, but their potential financial impact is not quantified in the supplied material (10-Q, L1312 and L1322).
The supplied filing references a separate Information Statement for additional risk factors; that document was not supplied and was not used.

insight.line: Insight: The $71.188 million operating cash outflow for the three months ended September 30, 2026 should not be read as recurring earnings burn alone: the 10-Q, L1510, states, “The increase was primarily due to changes in working capital assets and liabilities, and to a lesser extent, the change in net loss adjusted for non-cash items.”
insight.quote: Net cash used in operating activities for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased by $66,077 to $71,188. The increase was primarily due to changes in working capital assets and liabilities, and to a lesser extent, the change in net loss adjusted for non-cash items.
